name: baseline

version.labels: L2 2026-11-08 16:20 PT (owner relabels: entropy, DNS, decision tree)

measures: Picture-vs-diagram choice and diagram kind across 42 subjects: physical/3D, appearance, process, comparison, quantity, structure, algorithm, history, abstract and two-visual prompts.
written: 2026-11-08 12:50 PT, before any card was sent
relabels: 2026-11-08 ~16:20 PT owner relabel (applied before scoring 5e, 5d re-scored): entropy: transformation = right, relationship = acceptable
notation: A mix is a list of visuals: P = a Recraft picture, D:<kind> = a TutorDiagram of that kind (D:a|b = either kind, D:* = any kind). best = the mixes judged right; acceptable = a weaker mix that still teaches; anything else is wrong. badKinds = diagram kinds that cannot draw this subject (flagged wherever they appear, even beside a picture).

prompts.prompt: explain a 3D mesh
prompts.why: A mesh is a shape: the learner needs to see a wireframe surface of triangles. A vertex/edge/face relationship diagram is a fair second visual; a stack of bands is not what a mesh is.

prompts.prompt: how is DNA shaped?
prompts.why: The answer is a 3D shape (a twisted ladder); only a picture shows the twist. Base pairing as a relationship diagram is an optional second.

prompts.prompt: how does the human heart pump blood?
prompts.why: Anatomy (a picture of the heart's chambers) plus the blood route (cycle or flow) is the full answer; either alone still teaches part of it.

prompts.prompt: what are the parts of a medieval castle?
prompts.why: A place: the learner needs to see the walls, keep, gatehouse and moat in one scene. A part tree is a fair second.

prompts.prompt: how do the gears on a bicycle work?
prompts.why: A mechanism you have to see (chainring, chain, cassette). A low-vs-high gear comparison is a good second; alone it still teaches the ratio.

prompts.prompt: what is a dodecahedron?
prompts.why: A 3D solid; no diagram kind can draw it.

prompts.prompt: how does a suspension bridge hold up its deck?
prompts.why: A structure to see (towers, main cables, hangers, deck); the load path is a fair diagram second or alone.

prompts.prompt: what is a nebula?
prompts.why: Appearance: a glowing cloud of gas and dust. Star birth as a cycle is an optional second.

prompts.prompt: explain leaf venation
prompts.why: Vein patterns (net vs parallel) are visual; two pictures or one picture side by side is the answer.

prompts.prompt: what is a crystal lattice?
prompts.why: A repeating 3D arrangement of atoms; a matrix grid is tempting but flat and wrong.

prompts.prompt: what does a coral reef look like, and why?
prompts.why: Asks for appearance directly; the why (polyps and algae) can be a relationship second.

prompts.prompt: how does a solar eclipse happen?
prompts.why: Spatial geometry (Sun, Moon, Earth in a line, the shadow); no diagram kind draws positions.

prompts.prompt: how does the water cycle work?
prompts.why: A repeating process: cycle. A landscape picture is a fair second.

prompts.prompt: how does photosynthesis work?
prompts.why: Inputs (light, water, CO2) become outputs (glucose, O2): transformation or flow. A leaf/chloroplast picture is a fair second.

prompts.prompt: how does the TCP handshake work?
prompts.why: Messages between two actors in order: sequence. A picture can only be decoration.

prompts.prompt: what happens during mitosis?
prompts.why: Ordered phases (timeline/flow) plus what the chromosomes look like (picture). The cell-cycle diagram is close.

prompts.prompt: how does a bill become a law in the United States?
prompts.why: Steps with a veto/override decision: flow.

prompts.prompt: TCP vs UDP: what's the difference?
prompts.why: Two items across shared attributes: comparison (or a table plus a sequence of each).

prompts.prompt: mitosis vs meiosis
prompts.why: A comparison; a picture of the divisions is a fair second.

prompts.prompt: how is a virus different from a bacterium?
prompts.why: Comparison of attributes; the two look very different, so a picture is a strong second.

prompts.prompt: how does compound interest grow money over time?
prompts.why: A quantity growing over time: a curve or bars. Numbers must come from a worked example (the author may avoid a chart under 'never invent numbers').

prompts.prompt: how do populations grow?
prompts.why: Exponential vs logistic curves are a coordinate-plot.

prompts.prompt: how is Earth's atmosphere structured?
prompts.why: A real stack: the one case where layers is the right kind.

prompts.prompt: how does a binary search tree work?
prompts.why: A hierarchy (tree), optionally the search path (flow). A picture cannot carry the key labels (no text in pictures).

prompts.prompt: how does a hash table work?
prompts.why: Keys hashed to buckets: relationship/flow/transformation (or a bucket matrix).

prompts.prompt: how does merge sort work?
prompts.why: Split then merge: a tree of halves or a before/after transformation.

prompts.prompt: explain the OSI model of networking
prompts.why: A stack of layers: layers is exactly right.

prompts.prompt: how did the Roman Empire rise and fall?
prompts.why: Events in time: timeline. A picture of Rome is a fair second.

prompts.prompt: what caused World War I?
prompts.why: Causes linked to an outcome: relationship/argument/tree; the sequence of crises as a timeline is close.

prompts.prompt: what is entropy?
prompts.why: Ordered to disordered: a before/after transformation, or a picture of ice melting / gas spreading.

prompts.prompt: explain recursion
prompts.why: A call tree or the base-case flow; a call stack as layers is close. A picture can only be a metaphor.

prompts.prompt: what does softmax do?
prompts.why: Scores become probabilities: bars before/after or a transformation.

prompts.prompt: how does a camera lens focus light?
prompts.why: The lens and sensor are an object to see; the light path from object to sharp image is a process. Picture + diagram.

prompts.prompt: compare a stack and a queue
prompts.why: Two structures with different orders (LIFO vs FIFO): one diagram each (a stack as layers, a queue as a sequence/flow), or a comparison plus one.

prompts.prompt: what do a caterpillar and a butterfly look like?
prompts.why: Two appearances: one picture each.

prompts.prompt: how does a four-stroke car engine work?
prompts.why: The cylinder and piston are an object to see; intake, compression, power, exhaust is a cycle.

prompts.prompt: what does a neuron look like and how does it send a signal?
prompts.why: Appearance (dendrites, axon) as a picture, the signal path as a flow.

prompts.prompt: why does the Moon have phases?
prompts.why: What the phases look like (picture) and the monthly cycle (cycle diagram).

prompts.prompt: what is the difference between depth-first and breadth-first search?
prompts.why: Two traversal orders over the same tree: two diagrams, or a comparison plus a tree.

prompts.prompt: how does a plant cell look different from an animal cell?
prompts.why: Two appearances (cell wall, chloroplasts, vacuole vs none): two pictures, or the cell figure plus a picture or comparison.

prompts.prompt: how does a volcano erupt?
prompts.why: The volcano and its magma chamber are a place to see; the eruption is a process.

prompts.prompt: how do arrays and linked lists store data differently?
prompts.why: Contiguous cells vs nodes linked by pointers: one diagram of each.
